note: One entry per clip. 'segments' is the narration: one line per on-screen caption, in the order the captions appear in the scene.

segments.caption: Diffusion models learn to generate by learning to undo noise.
segments.text: Diffusion models learn to generate by learning to undo noise. We start from a real backbone, x zero, drawn here as sixteen C alpha points in a short helix. Training runs in two directions.

segments.caption: One forward step adds a little Gaussian noise to every point.
segments.text: The forward direction adds a little Gaussian noise at every step. Each point drifts by a random amount, and after the first few steps the helix is still obvious.

segments.caption: After t steps the result is one weighted mix of structure and noise.
segments.text: You never have to take the steps one at a time. After t steps, x t is a single weighted mix: the square root of the signal weight times x zero, plus the square root of one minus that weight, times one Gaussian draw.

segments.caption: The schedule sets those weights: at t = 500 the structure is nearly gone.
segments.text: The schedule fixes those weights. With beta rising from zero point zero zero zero one to zero point zero two over a thousand steps, the signal weight is zero point nine five at step one hundred, zero point seven two at two hundred fifty, and zero point two eight at five hundred.

segments.caption: By the last step nothing of the original structure is left.
segments.text: By step nine hundred ninety-nine the signal weight is zero point zero zero six: a Gaussian cloud. Every protein ends in the same place, which is exactly why sampling can start from noise alone.

segments.caption: Noising needs no learning, so training pairs are free.
segments.text: Noising needs no learning at all, just a random number generator. The network only ever learns the way back. One real structure gives a thousand training examples, one for every step.
